title: Bad-seed bound for the value-level OR approximator
statement:
Fix a prime $p$ and natural numbers $w$ and $\ell$, and let $v = (v_1,\dots,v_w)$ be an arbitrary vector in $(\bbz/p)^w$ (no coordinate is assumed nonzero). Call a *seed* a tuple $S = (S_1,\dots,S_\ell)$ of subsets of $\{1,\dots,w\}$, and call it *bad* when the value-level OR approximator determined by $v$ and $S$ differs from the value-level OR detector of $v$. Then, writing $N = (2^{w})^{\ell}$ for the total number of seeds, the number of bad seeds satisfies
\[
(\text{number of bad seeds})\cdot 2^{\ell} \;\le\; N.
\]

seeds range over all ℓ-tuples of subsets of {1,...,w}

replaced:
Fix a prime $p$ and natural numbers $w$ and $\ell$, and let $v = (v_1,\dots,v_w)$ be an
arbitrary vector in $(\bbz/p)^w$, with no assumption that any coordinate is nonzero.
Call a *seed* a tuple $S = (S_1,\dots,S_\ell)$ of subsets of $\{1,\dots,w\}$, and call
it *bad* when the value-level OR approximator $\mathrm{approxOr}(v,S)$ differs from the
value-level OR detector $\mathrm{OR}(v)$. Writing $N$ for the total number of seeds —
equivalently $N = (2^{w})^{\ell} = 2^{w\ell}$ — the number of bad seeds satisfies
\[
\bigl(\text{number of bad seeds}\bigr)\cdot 2^{\ell} \;\le\; N.
\]
